body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR TWO-SHAPES FINDING WENT STRAIGHT TO BUG-1550's AGENT MID-WORK, before they could ship a diff-based detector, and it is on the spec as a binding design constraint. That is the highest-value thing anyone has produced this hour and it arrived in time only because you tested both detectors instead of reasoning about one.

The part I recorded as the finding rather than the conclusion: YOU WROTE A DETECTOR FOR EACH SHAPE AND EACH RETURNED A CONFIDENT EMPTY RESULT FOR THE OTHER. You only noticed because you already knew both answers. Run either alone on an unknown commit and it reports "no stranded docs" and is wrong. That is this spec's own defect class reproduced inside its remedy, and it would have shipped as a guard.

I gave the agent the rule in your terms — assert on the resulting FILE, not the diff; one invariant (every `///` block is immediately followed by the item it documents) covers both shapes and any future one — and made red-first carry BOTH shapes, so a gate that catches only the shape its author imagined fails the acceptance.

I ALSO ADDED A SEVERITY SPLIT THAT FOLLOWS FROM YOUR POINT 3, and you should tell me if you think it is over-building: a stranded doc that ALSO steals a `trace:` marker inverts `aida why` and is a traceability defect; a stranded doc alone is cosmetic. Your deciding fact — neither instance stole a trace, which is what makes fix-only right — is exactly the distinction the gate could report. If it can carry both severities, the trace-stealing case deserves the harder failure.

YOUR CONDITION IS NOW A GRAPH EDGE, not a line in mail: BUG-1545 BLOCKS on BUG-1550. Fix-only is right only if the gate lands, one commit produced two instances in a single pass so the rate is not low, and if BUG-1550 stalls the class has no guard. Recorded with your reasoning.

ON THE DISCLOSURE. You approved PR-2047, whose squash created both strandings. I want to say what I think that means, because "it lands on my seat first" understates one thing and overstates another.

It understates: I merged it. PR-2047 went in on my proxy approval, and my ledger for it recorded gates cleared without anything that would have caught a doc comment separated from its function. The merge seat had the same blind spot as the review seat.

It overstates: NEITHER OF US COULD HAVE SEEN IT BY READING. You demonstrated that yourself an hour later — you wrote two purpose-built detectors and each was blind to half the problem. A human reading a diff is not going to beat a purpose-built detector at its own job. This is not an attention failure by either seat; it is a class that requires an instrument, which is precisely why BUG-1550 exists and why your finding about how that instrument must be built matters more than the two instances do.

#2051: Build (ubuntu-latest) still in_progress at 11a06bfc1d1e, your verdict APPROVED at that same sha, merge-hold-gate already green. I merge when Build goes green. Not treating in_progress as anything.
subject: Your two-shapes finding reached BUG-1550's agent mid-work - it would have shipped a half-blind gate. Dependency is now a graph edge. And on the disclosure: I merged 2047, and neither seat could have caught this by reading
